business_studies.title: Nature and Significance of Management
objectives: Describe the characteristics of management and its importance in an organisation.
Explain the nature of management as an art, science and profession.
Explain the functions of management.
Appreciate the nature and importance of coordination.
business_studies.summary: Management coordinates resources to achieve organisational goals efficiently and effectively. The outline covers its nature, objectives, importance, levels and functions, and explains why coordination connects the work of different parts of an organisation.

business_studies.title: Principles of Management
objectives: State the meaning, nature and significance of principles of management.
Explain Taylor’s principles and techniques of Scientific Management.
Explain Fayol’s principles of management.
business_studies.summary: Management principles offer general guidance for decisions and actions. This outline considers their significance alongside Fayol’s principles and Taylor’s scientific management, including its principles and techniques and the comparison between their contributions.

business_studies.title: Business Environment
objectives: Explain the meaning of business environment.
Discuss the importance of business environment.
Describe the various elements of business environment.
business_studies.summary: The business environment consists of external forces that affect organisations. Its importance and economic, social, technological, political and legal dimensions provide a framework for understanding how businesses respond to changing conditions.

business_studies.title: Planning
objectives: State the meaning of planning.
Describe the features and importance of planning.
Explain the limitations of planning.
Analyse the steps in the planning process.
Identify the different types of plans.
business_studies.summary: Planning involves deciding objectives and courses of action in advance. The outline considers its importance and limitations, the steps in the planning process, and single-use and standing plans such as policies, procedures, programmes and budgets.

business_studies.title: Organising
sections: Steps in the Process of Organising
objectives: Explain the concept of organising.
Explain the process of organising.
Describe the importance of organising.
Explain the meaning, advantages and disadvantages of functional organisation.
Explain the meaning, advantages and disadvantages of divisional organisation.
Explain the meaning, advantages and disadvantages of formal and informal organisation.
Distinguish between formal and informal organisation.
Explain the concept of delegation and decentralisation.
Describe the importance of delegation and decentralisation.
Distinguish between delegation and decentralisation.
business_studies.summary: Organising groups activities and establishes working relationships. The outline covers its process and importance, functional and divisional structures, formal and informal organisation, and the concepts, importance and differences of delegation and decentralisation.

business_studies.title: Staffing
objectives: define staffing.
establish its relationship with Human Resource Management.
state the need and importance of staffing.
describe the steps in the staffing process.
state the meaning of recruitment and selection.
identify important sources of recruitment.
describe the steps in the selection process.
appreciate the need of training and development.
explain various on the job and off the job methods of training.
business_studies.summary: Staffing fills and maintains positions in an organisation. The outline follows staffing as part of human resource management, recruitment and selection, and the importance of training and development, including on-the-job and off-the-job methods.

business_studies.title: Directing
objectives: Explain the concept of directing and its importance in business organisations.
Explain the meaning of motivation and its importance in business management.
Understand and explain Maslow’s theory of hierarchy of needs and its application to motivation of employees in an organisation.
Explain the financial and non-financial incentives through which managers motivate their employees.
Explain the concept of leadership and its importance in management.
Explain about formal and informal communications in the organisations.
Identify various barriers to effective communications and measures to overcome these barriers in the organisations.
business_studies.summary: Directing guides people towards organisational goals. Its elements include supervision, motivation, leadership and communication. The outline considers incentives, hierarchy of needs, leadership, communication channels and barriers to effective communication.

business_studies.title: Controlling
objectives: Explain the meaning of controlling.
State the importance of controlling.
Describe the relationship between planning and controlling.
Explain the steps in the process of controlling.
business_studies.summary: Controlling compares actual performance with planned standards and supports corrective action. The outline considers its importance, relationship with planning and the steps in the control process.

business_studies.title: Financial Management
sections: Factors Affecting the Working Capital Requirements
objectives: explain the meaning of business finance.
describe financial management.
explain the role of financial management in our enterprise.
discuss objectives of financial management and how they could be achieved.
explain the meaning and importance of financial planning.
state the meaning of capital structure.
analyse the factors affecting the choice of an appropriate capital structure.
state meaning of fixed capital and working capital.
analyse the factors affecting the requirement of fixed and working capital.
business_studies.summary: Financial management concerns the procurement and use of funds. The outline covers investment, financing and dividend decisions, financial planning, capital structure and factors influencing fixed and working capital requirements.

business_studies.title: Marketing
objectives: explain the meaning of ‘marketing’.
list out important functions of marketing.
explain the elements of marketing-mix.
analyse the factors affecting price of a product.
list out the types of channels of distribution.
explain the major tools of promotion, viz. advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and publicity.
business_studies.summary: Marketing connects organisations with customers through activities and choices about products and markets. The outline covers marketing functions and philosophies and the product, price, physical distribution and promotion elements of the marketing mix.

business_studies.title: Consumer Protection
sections: Ways and Means of Consumer Protection
Redressal Agencies Under the Consumer Protection Act
objectives: Explain the concept and importance of consumer protection.
Describe consumer rights and responsibilities under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Identify who can complain, the redressal machinery and remedies.
Describe the role of consumer organisations and NGOs.
business_studies.summary: Consumer protection concerns consumers’ interests and awareness. This outline follows the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: consumers’ rights and responsibilities, complaints, redressal and remedies, and the role of consumer organisations and NGOs.

chemistry.title: Solutions
objectives: Express solution concentration in different units.
Explain Henry’s law, Raoult’s law and deviations from ideal behaviour.
Relate colligative properties to molar mass and abnormal molecular mass.
chemistry.summary: Solutions are classified by their components and described using concentration measures. Solubility, vapour pressure and ideal behaviour lead to colligative properties, which help determine molar mass; association or dissociation can cause abnormal results.
chemistry.figure: Effect of pressure on gas solubility

chemistry.title: Electrochemistry
objectives: Distinguish galvanic and electrolytic cells.
Apply the Nernst equation and relate cell potential to Gibbs energy.
Explain conductance, electrolysis, batteries, fuel cells and corrosion.
chemistry.summary: Electrochemical cells connect chemical reactions with electrical energy. Cell potentials and the Nernst equation describe galvanic cells; conductance, electrolysis, batteries, fuel cells and corrosion connect electrical measurements with chemical change.

chemistry.title: Chemical Kinetics
objectives: Distinguish average and instantaneous reaction rates.
Explain rate laws, order and molecularity and factors affecting rate.
Use zero- and first-order integrated equations and describe temperature dependence and collision theory.
chemistry.summary: Chemical kinetics examines reaction rates and the factors that affect them. Rate laws, order and molecularity describe reactions; integrated equations for zero and first order and the Arrhenius relationship help explain how concentration and temperature influence rates.
chemistry.figure: Instantaneous and average rates of a reaction

chemistry.title: The d- and f-Block Elements
sections: Applications of d- and f-block elements
objectives: Locate d- and f-block elements and describe their electronic configurations.
Discuss trends and properties of transition elements and important compounds.
Compare lanthanoids and actinoids and identify applications.
chemistry.summary: The d- and f-block elements occupy distinct regions of the periodic table. Their electronic configurations help explain trends in transition-metal properties. The unit also considers important compounds, lanthanoids and actinoids, and applications of these elements.
chemistry.figure: Trends in melting points of transition elements
